title: Reinstatement Terms After Non-Payment, Pass and Trip Protection
content:
Where cover under a Pass and Trip Protection plan has stopped because an instalment of premium went unpaid,
whether it may be put back in force at all, what that costs and how long the household has to ask are fixed by
the plan. The three figures are scheduled here.

| Plan | Cover may be put back in force | Fee for putting cover back in force (USD) | Window after cover stops (calendar days) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Season Pass Protection Basic | No | 0.00 | 0 |
| Season Pass Protection Plus | Yes | 25.00 | 30 |
| Season Pass Protection Premier | Yes | 25.00 | 45 |
| Collective Trip Protection Standard | No | 0.00 | 0 |
| Collective Trip Protection Elite | Yes | 45.00 | 45 |
| Collective Total Protection Concierge | Yes | 0.00 | 90 |

**On the two plans that allow none.** Season Pass Protection Basic and Collective Trip Protection Standard
carry no reinstatement at all, which is why each shows a fee of 0.00 USD and a window of 0 days; a figure of
zero on those rows records the absence of the entitlement and not a free reinstatement.

**On the four that allow it.** The fee stands at 25.00 USD on Season Pass Protection Plus and Season Pass
Protection Premier and at 45.00 USD on Collective Trip Protection Elite; the Collective Total Protection
Concierge plan charges nothing, at 0.00 USD, and carries the longest window at 90 calendar days. The window
runs 30 days on Season Pass Protection Plus and 45 days on both Season Pass Protection Premier and Collective
Trip Protection Elite.
